item.title: Beyond the deal: The achievable path to Ukrainian victory
item.description: One of the key strategic questions of the current war amounts to is this war winnable? Experts are increasingly saying that Russia cannot win. However, can Ukraine win? Artykuł Beyond the deal: The achievable path to Ukrainian victory pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: Prisoners for potash: Alyaksandr Lukashenka and the GDR precedent
item.description: Minsk’s recent decision to release high-profile prisoners has been underpinned by US moves to relax sanctions concerning the export of potash. While this may well appear like a genuine thaw in relations, it ultimately resembles a tried-and-tested tactic by dictatorships close to Russia to use prisoners as a bargaining chip. Artykuł Prisoners for potash: Alyaksandr Lukashenka and the GDR precedent pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: Russia’s river strategy is the next Eurasian power shift
item.description: While the world’s gaze is fixed on Donald Trump and if he can broker peace in Ukraine, Moscow is quietly launching a far bigger game. As Washington obsesses over Beijing, Russia is weaving together rivers, railways, and drone corridors into a new logistics superpower, aiming not just to recover from sanctions but to dominate the Eurasian continent. item.title: The Balkans in the multipolar moment
item.description: Wider shifts in the global order are challenging the foreign policy trajectories of Balkan states. While expectations have existed of a clear integration into western structures, the current reality reveals a variety of relationships with powers outside the region. Credible action by the West is necessary if a feasible model of development is to persist among local states. Artykuł The Balkans in the multipolar moment pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: The US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations: Architecture of tactical theatre and strategic deception
item.description: The road to a negotiated settlement between Ukraine and Russia still remains unclear. While representatives continue to meet in various formats, the core demands of both sides show little sign of changing. A frozen conflict scenario subsequently becomes a very real possibility. item.title: Bulgaria at the rule of law crossroads: can Rumen Radev become the much-needed game changer?
item.description: The ongoing saga relating to corruption in Bulgaria has taken a new turn with the resignation of President Rumen Radev. The long-term critic of the political establishment has now decided to enter parliament in hopes of curtailing the country’s rule of law backsliding. Polls suggest that the former president could well command significant support but some commentators worry if Radev will manage to deliver on his promises. item.title: Empty towers: inside Tirana’s mad construction boom
item.description: The Albanian capital is undergoing (and suffering) extremely rapid urban transformation, involving major players in contemporary architecture. Against all reason, prices have skyrocketed, while most of the buildings remain empty. Artykuł Empty towers: inside Tirana’s mad construction boom pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.
